questions.stem: A student sets up three test tubes each containing an iron nail: Tube A has air and water, Tube B has boiled water sealed with oil, and Tube C has dry air with a desiccant. After one week, which tube(s) will show rusting?

options.text: All three tubes
Only Tube A
Tubes A and B
Tubes A and C

questions.explanation: Rusting requires both oxygen AND water. Tube A has both, so the nail rusts. Tube B has water but the boiled water has had dissolved oxygen removed and the oil prevents oxygen entering, so no rusting. Tube C has air (oxygen) but the desiccant removes moisture, so no rusting. Only Tube A provides both conditions.

questions.stem: A ship's hull is made of steel and has blocks of zinc bolted to it below the waterline. How does this prevent the hull from rusting?

options.text: Zinc is waterproof and physically blocks water from reaching the steel
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes preferentially, protecting the iron (sacrificial protection)
Zinc reacts with the salt water to create a protective acid layer
Zinc absorbs oxygen from the water so there is none left to rust the iron

questions.explanation: This is sacrificial protection. Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it oxidises (corrodes) preferentially instead of the iron. The zinc loses electrons more readily and effectively 'sacrifices' itself to protect the steel. The zinc blocks need to be replaced periodically as they are consumed.

questions.stem: A bicycle chain is oiled regularly to prevent rusting. What method of rust prevention does this represent?

options.text: Sacrificial protection
Barrier method - the oil prevents water and oxygen reaching the iron
Galvanising
Alloying

questions.explanation: Oiling is a barrier method of rust prevention. The oil creates a physical coating that prevents water and oxygen from coming into contact with the iron surface. Without both water and oxygen, rusting cannot occur. Sacrificial protection uses a more reactive metal; galvanising specifically uses zinc coating; alloying changes the metal composition.

questions.stem: Stainless steel, used for cutlery and surgical instruments, does not rust even though it contains iron. Why is this?

options.text: Stainless steel does not contain any iron
The chromium in stainless steel forms a tough, unreactive oxide layer that protects the iron
Stainless steel is coated with plastic
The nickel in stainless steel acts as a sacrificial metal

questions.explanation: Stainless steel is an alloy containing iron, chromium (and often nickel). The chromium reacts with oxygen to form a very thin but extremely tough and adherent chromium oxide layer on the surface. This layer is self-healing and prevents water and oxygen from reaching the iron underneath, stopping rust from forming.

questions.stem: Iron gates are often galvanised (coated with zinc). If the zinc coating gets scratched, exposing the iron underneath, the iron still does not rust immediately. Why?

options.text: The scratch seals itself because zinc is self-healing
Iron is unreactive when exposed to small amounts of air
The nearby zinc acts as sacrificial protection, corroding instead of the exposed iron
The scratch allows water to drain away from the iron surface

questions.explanation: Galvanising provides two types of protection. The zinc coating acts as a barrier, but even when scratched, the zinc provides sacrificial protection. Because zinc is more reactive than iron, the zinc near the scratch corrodes preferentially, protecting the exposed iron. This is a key advantage of galvanising over other barrier methods like painting.
